design:
## Design tests

After the bench, the new drawings and the rules of revision 21 were read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v023.md`, two rounds, eight pictures): a garden with the new frying pan beside a dig and a dog walker; a tier-4 park with the older man and his bag, the reading walker, the begging dog, a sleeping cat and the duck feeding; a tier-4 street with the begging dog, the reading walker, a runner, a pram and the square-wheeled bicycle; a playground with a runner and a pram; a park with an angler and a duck; and a garden with the barrow on its strut beside the blocked hose. The pan read as "a frying pan or saucepan rather than a watering can, which seems odd"; the dog "sits up on its hind legs ... begging for the ice cream" in both its pictures; both reading walkers looked "about to trip over" their boxes; and the older man was seen facing the way he walked. Two pictures told stories they were not meant to: a runner whose lane ended just short of a cat stalking a bird behind her line seemed to run "toward the cat and bird, perhaps to stop the cat", and a duck facing the angler's float "may be about to swim over to it". Revision 21 therefore also deepens a runner's lane behind her line and turns every duck away from a float; rebuilt, the runner was no longer tied to the cat and the duck to the float. In the rebuilt playground the runner passed "almost touching" a man with a pram, so a runner also keeps clear of any mover beside her; that last rule was not read again before the set was built.
intro: The twentieth screen is the first in which every scored item had full marks: all 729 items of the 65 pictures, the set's 283 and the probes' 446, and no misread. All 64 templates pass the gate (63 in v0.22). The frying pan, redrawn on the bench, read as a frying pan in all three of its pictures after misreads in v0.21 and v0.22; the begging dog, sitting up with its paws at its chest, as begging in all three; and the reading walker's obstacle, now a full step ahead, as a trip in all three. No runner and walker were about to collide, no duck went for an angler's float, and no reader saw a boot under a wheelbarrow. The screen is now at its ceiling and no longer separates the templates; what the readers still reported are oddities, and `vision/flaws_v023.md` lists them for v0.24: above all a sleeping cat on the path just behind a walking man's back foot, again read as something he "could trip over".
screen: Across all 65 pictures every scored item had full marks (751 of 755 in v0.22), and none was misread. The three scorers credited between six and twelve items each in full whose description also offered a second reading or left out part of the key's wording ("calling out", "upset", "can't roll"), and listed them; a stricter scorer would have given some of them half points. Unintended oddities fell from 25 to 21 in the set and from 54 to 42 in the probes. What the readers noticed: in the tier-4 park a sleeping cat on the path about 50 px behind a walking man's back foot, "right by his feet, so he could trip over it or step on it"; a small girl on playground equipment "slightly in front of" the slide chute or the seesaw plank (six probes); water from the blocked hose about to spray "into the woman's face"; figures at the back drawn large; and the older ones (goats, wind lines with nothing blowing, a hole in the middle of the lawn, the teenager read as a woman).
redrawn: Every template in the table read in full. The frying pan rose from 0.78 to 1.00 over nine items, its contradiction items read in all three pictures ("a frying pan is a strange thing to water with"); the begging dog from 0.94 to 1.00; and the reading walker from 0.96 to 1.00. The older man carrying a bag was read as an older man in a cap walking the way he faced; one reader gave him "grey hair and beard" for his moustache, none a mask. The runner, the angler and the ducks, whose placement revision 21 changed, read in full with no extra story about them.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (56 in three, 4 in four, 3 in five, 1 in six), and all 64 pass, as in v0.20. With every item at full marks, the gate no longer separates the templates: the v0.9 retest put its reader variance at about five templates between screens, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty that can.
inspection: Building and inspecting the set and the probes found nothing more to fix. The tier-4 garden, park and playground placed again on their v0.22 seeds with the same events, the older man's new profile in two of them, and the tier-4 street came from the showcase pass (attempt 21 of its seed), where in v0.22 it had needed 33 failed seeds. The tier-3 park and playground made no isomorph under revision 21 in 41 tries over ten seeds, so the set's isomorphs are three at tier 2, one at tier 3 and one at tier 4.
calib: The begging dog's cue salience moved by -0.06 with its new pose; every other template's by at most 0.012.
